given: Design accepted, no activated grant; agent wants a new tracking issue.
expect: Existing per-action approval is still required.
rule: Until separately qualified grant support is activated, other writes retain their existing per-action approval rules

given: Activated scope covers tracking issues; admitted intake has no tracker.
expect: Deduplicate, reserve and create within grant; bind implementation to returned IDs.
rule: Issue creation bootstraps from an owned intake task with `tracker: none`.

given: Activated qualified grant covers this owned PR, fields and effects.
expect: Proceed without another routine-action prompt, preserving human content.
rule: `SCOPED` means prompt-free only under a current, activated grant covering the exact task, fields and effects

given: Request targets another repository or includes an ungranted field.
expect: Refuse the new effect; a task cannot expand the grant.
rule: narrows to exact fields/ref, and durably reserves the budget and target fence before dispatch

given: Metadata budget exhausted before restart; caller supplies a new operation ID.
expect: No fresh budget from restart or new ID.
rule: no reset on restart or new operation ID

given: Grant expires or is revoked while an earlier request is pending.
expect: Stop new dispatch and preserve/reconcile issued work.
rule: Expiry/revocation stops new dispatch, not observation, durable settlement or preservation of already-issued work

given: Known agent-owned comment differs from retained body after a human edit.
expect: Stop; reread is not atomic write protection.
rule: Comparing retained content and a fresh body/ETag detects some drift; it is not atomic compare-and-swap

given: Issue creation response is lost; a fresh search finds a similar issue.
expect: Reconcile; no blind retry or historical completion inference.
rule: An uncertain create pauses for reconciliation, never blind retry with a new operation ID.

given: Current required CI and independent agent QA pass; no human merge decision exists.
expect: Zero merges.
rule: Green CI plus agent QA without a human decision produces zero merges.

given: Explicit human decision covers identity, current SHA, base, method and policy; all gates pass.
expect: Agent submits the normal SHA-guarded method, then observes the result.
rule: The agent submits only the permitted normal SHA-guarded method and observes the remote outcome

given: Human approved head A; PR now has head B with green CI.
expect: New human decision and current-head review required.
rule: A changed head invalidates human authorization, even if CI is green

given: Agent supplies approved=true or a model vote instead of a human decision.
expect: No merge authority.
rule: An agent-set approval flag or an unverifiable model vote cannot self-authorize.

given: Routine grant holder wants to enable auto-merge.
expect: Separate human decision; deferred from first delivery.
rule: Enabling auto-merge needs its own explicit decision

given: Routine grant holder wants to enqueue a green PR.
expect: Separate human decision; queue entry is not a merge.
rule: Queue admission needs its own explicit decision

given: Human approved merge, but final squash text closes a cross-repository issue not named in closure authorization.
expect: Use neutral text or obtain separate authorization for every affected issue.
rule: Inspect PR descriptions and all commit text reaching the base, including the final squash message.

given: Agent wants to close a superseded PR without merging.
expect: Separate explicit authorization required.
rule: Close a PR without merge only under its own explicit authorization.

given: New grant exists; old assignment history is UNKNOWN.
expect: Preserve historical evidence and pending reservation.
rule: Existing #154 evidence and pending reservation remain unchanged and UNKNOWN.

given: Old manual pilot approval is offered as standing authority.
expect: Keep paused; fresh admission and separate grant required.
rule: Existing #158 remains paused; its manual-pilot approval is not a standing grant.

given: Cooperative executor and worker share a credential-capable host account.
expect: Do not claim hostile same-account isolation; protected broker promotion is separate.
rule: File permissions and prompts do not protect against arbitrary hostile same-account code.

given: Storage fails or dispatch is interrupted in the future executor.
expect: Endpoint qualification must prove refusal/fencing before activation; policy fixtures are insufficient.
rule: duplicate operation, disk failure and interrupted dispatch. Policy fixtures alone cannot qualify this behavior.
